title: Sum of a Rectangle

concept.title: Two-dimensional prefix sums
body: Let `p[i][j]` be the sum of all cells in the rectangle from the top left corner to row `i`, column `j`. It can be built with inclusion and exclusion: add the cell, add the rectangle above and the rectangle on the left, and subtract the part counted twice.
A query for the rectangle with corners `(r1, c1)` and `(r2, c2)` then takes the big prefix rectangle and removes the strips above and to the left, adding back the corner that was removed twice:

statement: You are given a matrix with `n` rows and `m` columns and `q` queries. A query gives `r1 c1 r2 c2` (counting from 1): the sum of all cells in rows `r1..r2` and columns `c1..c2` is asked. Print the answer to each query.
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `m` integers each.
Each of the next `q` lines has `r1 c1 r2 c2`.
outputFormat: Print `q` lines, one answer per query.

examples.note: The whole matrix sums to 45; the lower right block 5 6 8 9 sums to 28.

hints: Build a table `p` with one extra row and column of zeros.
Each `p[i][j]` is the cell plus the prefix above, plus the prefix on the left, minus the corner counted twice.

explanation: A table of 2-D prefix sums is built once. Every rectangle sum is then a combination of four table entries.
solution.complexity: Time O(n * m + q), space O(n * m).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m, q = map(int, input().split())
g = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
qs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

p = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    for j in range(1, m + 1):
        p[i][j] = g[i - 1][j - 1] + p[i - 1][j] + p[i][j - 1] - p[i - 1][j - 1]
out = []
for r1, c1, r2, c2 in qs:
    out.append(p[r2][c2] - p[r1 - 1][c2] - p[r2][c1 - 1] + p[r1 - 1][c1 - 1])
print("\n".join(map(str, out)))
